chains.title: Ref T preserves an ARID5B repressor motif in the FTO intron-1 enhancer; alt C disrupts it, derepressing IRX3/IRX5 and shifting adipocytes from beige to white
chains.element: dELS cCRE EH38E3181208 in FTO intron 1 (chr16:53766999-53767220), the rs1421085 conserved cis-regulatory module
chains.cell_type: Adipocyte progenitor / beige adipocyte, subcutaneous adipose

links.claim: ARID5B is not in QBiC-SELEX coverage (E18), so no QBiC binding change can be cited for it; instead, published work states that the T-to-C change interrupts a conserved ARID5B repressor motif, i.e. the ref T allele supports binding and the alt C does not (E20a). The site is modestly conserved (GERP 2.55, E01), consistent with a functional motif. I do not cite any other TF's QBiC score as evidence for ARID5B.

The variant lies inside a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E3181208); the quoted DNase/H3K27ac z-scores are maxima over biosamples and belong to the neighbouring EH38E3181207, so adipose-specific activity is not shown by ENCODE here. Independent evidence that this sequence is a functional cis-regulatory module comes from mouse deletion of the rs1421085 CRM (E20c).

Deletion of the rs1421085 CRM in mice changes Irx3 and Irx5 expression and adipocyte mitochondrial function (E20c), and IRX3 overexpression raises Ucp1 (E20d, E20e), so IRX3/IRX5 ~520 kb away (E02) are the mechanistic targets even though L2G assigns FTO 0.99 and IRX3 no score (E05) and no adipose eQTL exists for any gene at this variant (E19: FTO in muscle, IRX3 in pancreas only, both alt-increasing).
The effect is observed in human abdominal subcutaneous-derived beige adipocytes and adipocyte progenitors; bulk GTEx subcutaneous adipose is used only as an expression proxy, which is a limitation.

Loss of ARID5B repression raises IRX3/IRX5 and lowers thermogenic gene expression (UCP1, PM20D1, CIDEA) and proton-leak respiration in CC carriers (E20b), reducing energy expenditure and producing the very strong BMI/obesity and downstream T2D/HbA1c associations (E04, E06b, E06c). Note a direction discrepancy: GWAS Catalog lists T as the effect allele (E04) whereas the functional literature identifies C as the obesity-risk allele (E20b); the catalog allele annotation at this locus should not be taken at face value.

predictions: EMSA/allele-specific ARID5B ChIP in preadipocytes shows stronger occupancy on T than on C
Isogenic C-to-T editing at this single base lowers IRX3/IRX5 and raises UCP1/mitochondrial respiration in adipocytes
ARID5B knockdown in TT cells phenocopies the CC state (higher IRX3/IRX5, lower UCP1)
Allelic luciferase/MPRA: C shows higher enhancer activity than T in preadipocytes, and the difference is lost on ARID5B knockdown
FTO mRNA in subcutaneous adipose is not consistently genotype-dependent (consistent with E19 showing no adipose eQTL)
falsified_if: ARID5B binds both alleles equally, or ARID5B knockdown does not change IRX3/IRX5
Single-base C-to-T editing leaves IRX3/IRX5 and thermogenic genes unchanged
CRM deletion changes FTO but not IRX3/IRX5 in adipocytes

chains.title: Alt C creates a stronger TALE-homeodomain (TGIF1/TGIF2/MEIS) site that activates the intron-1 enhancer
chains.element: dELS cCRE EH38E3181208 in FTO intron 1

links.claim: QBiC group G008 (TALE homeodomain) shows a large, fully consistent alt-allele gain across 9 models (best model PKNOX2 own model, z 54.71, effect +3.05; site 95.5th to 99.7th percentile). The group names a shared specificity, not one TF; I pick TGIF1 because it is the most expressed covered member in subcutaneous adipose (13.07 TPM), with TGIF2 (11.62), MEIS3 (9.23) and PKNOX1 (7.35) nearly as plausible. This is an in vitro prediction only.
The gained site falls in a distal enhancer-like cCRE that mouse CRM deletion shows is a functional regulatory module, though ENCODE gives no adipose-specific signal here.
The CRM regulates IRX3/IRX5 (E20c); L2G instead favours FTO (0.99) and there is no adipose eQTL for either gene (E19), so the gene link rests on the mouse CRM result, not on this variant's own QTL.
TGIF1/TGIF2/MEIS factors are expressed in bulk subcutaneous adipose at the listed TPMs; no preadipocyte footprint or occupancy data is cited.

If a gained TALE activator site raises enhancer output and IRX3/IRX5, the C allele would lower thermogenesis and raise BMI, matching the reported lower thermogenic capacity of CC carriers (E20b) and the locus BMI/obesity signal (E04).

predictions: TGIF1/TGIF2 or MEIS ChIP in preadipocytes shows allele-biased occupancy favouring C
Knockdown of TGIF1/TGIF2 (not ARID5B) abolishes the allelic reporter difference
A TALE-family footprint is detectable at this site in adipose DNase data
falsified_if: No TALE-family occupancy or footprint at the site in adipose cells
TALE knockdown leaves allelic enhancer activity unchanged while ARID5B knockdown abolishes it

chains.title: Alt C strengthens an ERR half-site bound by ESRRA, altering oxidative-program enhancer output
chains.element: dELS cCRE EH38E3181208 in FTO intron 1

links.claim: QBiC group G037 gives the strongest signal in the screen (best model ESRRG own model, z 62.01, effect +2.15; all 3 models same sign; site 94.0th to 99.7th percentile). Within this shared ERR specificity only ESRRA is appreciably expressed in subcutaneous adipose (34.08 TPM vs ESRRG 0.06, ESRRB 0.16), so ESRRA is the named TF; it is covered through a mapped model (z 17.39), not its own best model. Prediction only, no occupancy data.
The created half-site lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE shown by mouse deletion to be a functional CRM; ENCODE biosample-specific adipose signal is not available.
The CRM modulates IRX3/IRX5 (E20c); ESRRA regulation of these genes is not demonstrated, and no adipose eQTL exists (E19).
ESRRA is well expressed in bulk subcutaneous adipose (34.08 TPM); preadipocyte occupancy is not shown.
If ERR binding on C alters enhancer output toward IRX3/IRX5 and away from thermogenesis, it would reproduce the lower thermogenic capacity of CC adipocytes and the BMI/HbA1c associations.

predictions: ESRRA ChIP-seq shows allele-biased occupancy at chr16:53767042 favouring C
ESRRA knockdown or inverse agonist removes the allelic reporter difference
Allelic effect is larger in differentiated, mitochondria-rich adipocytes than in progenitors
falsified_if: ESRRA shows no occupancy at this cCRE in any biosample
Reporter activity is unchanged by ESRRA perturbation but changed by ARID5B knockdown

grades_v0.reason: ARID5B has no cited evidence; E01 gives only intron consequence and GERP 2.55. No QBiC, ChIP or motif data. Repressor role and ref-allele preference are asserted from memory.

E03 shows a dELS cCRE overlapping the variant with max-over-biosample DNase/H3K27ac (the signal values are for the neighbouring cCRE EH38E3181207, not this one) and no adipose-specific z-scores. Consistent with an enhancer but indirect.
E02 puts IRX3 520 kb away, and E05 gives IRX3 no L2G score while FTO scores 0.99. No eQTL, Hi-C or CRISPR evidence supports IRX3/IRX5; the same-TAD claim is uncited. Cited evidence points to FTO.

E08 and E10 are QBiC groups for ESRR and NR4A, irrelevant to ARID5B or to preadipocytes. Nothing cited shows ARID5B expression or enhancer activity in preadipocytes; the context is only bulk subcutaneous adipose.
E04, E06b, E06c and E06e establish the variant's association with BMI and obesity, but not the IRX3/IRX5 energy-expenditure mechanism or any ARID5B role.

E09 shows a strong, consistent alt gain across 9 models (z 54.71, best model PKNOX2), but it is a binding prediction only. Picking TGIF1 on TPM is a defensible reason, though TGIF2, MEIS and PKNOX1 are equally plausible. The title and claim treat TGIF1/MEIS1 loosely, and the best model is PKNOX2 (2.8 TPM).
E03 gives a dELS cCRE with maximum DNase/H3K27ac values that belong to the neighbouring cCRE; there is no adipose-specific signal and no footprint.
E05 supports FTO as the L2G gene (0.99), which is a statistical rather than regulatory link. IRX3 is the declared target but has no cited support, and the claim mixes IRX3 and FTO.
E09 gives TPM values from bulk subcutaneous adipose, which shows expression only; there is no preadipocyte evidence or occupancy.
E04 and E06c support a locus-level BMI/obesity association, not this TF or mechanism. Adipocyte differentiation is asserted without citation.

E08 shows a very strong alt gain in a consistent ESRR group, but ESRRA is chosen from the group by TPM, which is reasonable. The best model is ESRRG (0.06 TPM), and ESRRA is covered via mapped models with z 17.39. It remains a binding prediction only.
E03 shows a dELS cCRE but no adipose-specific signal; the claim of an 'adipose' enhancer is not shown.
E05 supports FTO via L2G, but IRX3 has no support and ESRRA regulation of either gene is not shown. The claim lumps FTO/IRX3 together.
E08 gives ESRRA 34 TPM in bulk subcutaneous adipose. Expression is consistent, but the oxidative-program role is from memory and there is no preadipocyte data.
E04 supports the locus-level association only, with no link to ERR activity. HbA1c is covered by E04, but the mechanism is uncited.

E10 shows alt gain in a broad NR group where members disagree on direction. The best model is NR4A3, and NR4A1 is chosen only by TPM among 38+ covered TFs, which is a weak reason. This is a binding prediction only.
E03 gives a dELS cCRE; the claim of 'adipose-relevant biosamples' is not supported because biosample-specific z-scores are absent.

E05 gives FTO L2G 0.99, and the variant is intronic to FTO (E01), so FTO is the best-supported gene statistically. No eQTL (0 molecular QTL credible sets) or perturbation supports regulation of FTO expression.
E10 gives NR4A1 expression of 139.74 TPM in bulk subcutaneous adipose, which is consistent but indirect; NR4A1 is an immediate-early gene.
E04 and E06c support the association only. The m6A-dependent program is asserted without cited evidence linking to this variant.

grades_final.reason: ARID5B is not in QBiC coverage and the chain correctly cites no other TF's score. The only support is a literature statement (E20a) that T-to-C interrupts a conserved ARID5B motif. That is a motif claim, not a shown allele-specific binding assay in the quoted evidence. GERP 2.55 is only modest context.

The variant lies in dELS cCRE EH38E3181208 (E03), but the activity z-scores belong to the neighbouring cCRE and are maxima across biosamples, so no adipose-specific activity is shown. The mouse CRM deletion (E20c) shows the CRM is functional but is not direct evidence for this human element.

E20c shows the CRM deletion changes Irx3/Irx5 in mouse adipocytes, which is perturbation evidence but cross-species and for the whole CRM. Against it, L2G gives FTO 0.99 and IRX3 no score, and the only IRX3 eQTL is in pancreas. E20d and E20e concern IRX3 function, not regulation by this variant. The chain acknowledges the conflict.

E20a and E20b are human subcutaneous-derived beige adipocytes carrying the genotype, which is a relevant cell type for the phenotype. The quotes do not show ARID5B binding or IRX3 changes in progenitors, and the chain itself says GTEx bulk adipose is only a proxy.

E20b shows lower thermogenic gene expression and proton leak in CC beige adipocytes, and E04, E06b and E06c show strong obesity association. The link from ARID5B derepression and IRX3/5 to energy expenditure and BMI is inferred, not shown. The chain notes that E04 lists T as the effect allele, opposite to the claimed C risk allele, and this direction conflict is not resolved by the cited evidence.

QBiC G008 shows a consistent alt-allele gain, but it is in vitro prediction only. TGIF1 was chosen by TPM among many group members, which is reasoned but not specific. TGIF1 is not the best or own model; the mapped models are not individually shown.
The variant lies in a dELS cCRE (E03), and E20c supports the CRM being functional in mouse. No adipose-specific activity or occupancy is shown, and nothing ties a TALE site to enhancer activity.
E20c links the CRM to Irx3/Irx5 in mouse, but L2G favours FTO and there is no adipose eQTL. The link is independent of the proposed TF and rests on the CRM result alone.
Only bulk GTEx expression for the group members is cited (E09), which is expression context. No preadipocyte data, footprint or occupancy is cited.

Reference to E20b and E04 shows the phenotype exists, but the chain is conditional ("if a gained activator site..."). The mechanism from TALE binding to phenotype is hypothetical, and E04 gives T as the effect allele, which is not reconciled.

QBiC G037 has the strongest z-score with alt gain, but this is in vitro prediction only. ESRRA was chosen for its expression among the group's TFs, with a mapped model at z 17.39 rather than its own best model. No occupancy data is cited.
The variant lies in a dELS cCRE (E03) and the mouse CRM deletion supports a functional CRM (E20c). There is no adipose-specific signal and no evidence for ERR involvement at this element.
E20c supports the CRM regulating Irx3/Irx5, but the chain itself says ESRRA regulation of these genes is not demonstrated. L2G favours FTO and there is no adipose eQTL.
ESRRA expression of 34 TPM in bulk subcutaneous adipose is expression context only. No preadipocyte occupancy is shown.
The chain is conditional ("if ERR binding alters output"). E20b and E04 show the phenotype but give no link to ESRRA. The T-versus-C direction discrepancy in E04 is not addressed.

checks.why: Shows whether the variant is an eQTL for IRX3, FTO or RPGRIP1L in adipose, which would separate the IRX3 chains from the FTO chain.
Establishes whether ARID5B is in QBiC coverage and which allele it prefers; H1 currently has no binding evidence.
Tests whether ESRRA occupies this site in any biosample, which is the strongest available test of the top-scoring QBiC group.
